title: How to use AI for startup investing
description: Use Strawberry across market intelligence, deal flow, investment decisions, introductions, and portfolio monitoring.

navigation.title: Venture Capital & Investing
navigation.tagline: Markets, deal flow, decisions, and portfolio support

introduction: Venture work rarely lives in one system. Market research, founder conversations, pipeline notes, data rooms, portfolio updates, and the firm's own investment history can all shape the next decision.

Strawberry works across those sources in the browser alongside the investor. It can inspect current company information and logged-in tools, connect them with the firm's thesis and prior decisions, and keep that context available as the work moves from sourcing to meetings, diligence, memos, and portfolio support.

blocks.text: Not sure where to begin? Your companion can look at the investment work you have open and suggest a useful skill to try first.

skill.context: Use the investment work and context already in front of you to choose a useful first Venture Capital skill.

blocks.text: A startup map should explain how a market is taking shape, not merely return a list of companies. Strawberry can follow current company pages, funding announcements, investor portfolios, accelerator cohorts, logged-in databases, hiring, and news while keeping source dates beside the findings.

That makes it easier to compare what investors say they focus on with where they have actually invested, spot clusters and white space, and connect the landscape back to the firm's thesis and pass history.

blocks.text: Deal sourcing has a natural progression, but each step answers a different question. Which companies fit the thesis? Which deserve more time? Where has the process stalled? Strawberry can carry the evidence forward without blurring those decisions together.

items.title: Source against the firm's thesis
items.text: Start with a varied, evidence-backed set that can be corrected before the search expands.

skill.context: Turn the firm's thesis into a calibrated, sourced set of companies worth reviewing.

items.title: Research the companies that stand out
items.text: Build a concise view of the company, thesis fit, tensions, recent changes, and unanswered questions.

skill.context: Build a source-linked company view with preliminary thesis fit, tensions, and next questions.

items.title: Review where the pipeline needs attention
items.text: Compare the CRM with recent meetings, messages, and diligence to find stale records, missing next steps, and decisions that have stalled.

skill.context: Review active opportunities using the firm's actual stages, decision rules, and recent context.

blocks.text: The next move may depend on a credible relationship path or an accurate CRM record. Strawberry can inspect the evidence for the connection, prepare the appropriate ask, and propose the exact record changes without treating either as part of the research by default.

items.title: Make a warm introduction
items.text: Verify the relationship path and prepare a considerate intermediary ask or double opt-in.

skill.context: Find a credible network path and prepare the appropriate introduction or intermediary ask.

items.title: Keep the investment CRM current
items.text: Prepare and verify changes using the firm's real objects, stages, and source-of-truth rules.

skill.context: Apply reviewed investment-record changes using the team's real CRM schema.

blocks.text: Founder calls, expert conversations, diligence, and the investment memo should build on the same company record. Strawberry can prepare from the calendar and relationship history, preserve what was actually learned, and keep the supporting sources close as the firm tests the case.

items.title: Prepare for the conversation
items.text: Bring together the company history, people, open questions, and recent evidence for a founder, partner, or expert meeting.

skill.context: Prepare for a founder, partner, expert, board, or portfolio conversation.

items.title: Capture what changed
items.text: Turn a reliable record into evidence, commitments, questions, and the follow-through that needs review.

skill.context: Turn the reliable meeting record into evidence, commitments, questions, and follow-through.

items.title: Test the important questions
items.text: Use appropriately deep diligence to investigate the claims and risks that could change the decision.

skill.context: Test the claims and risks that could change the investment decision.

items.title: Write the investment memo
items.text: Bring the case, counterevidence, risks, and open questions into a source-linked decision record.

skill.context: Turn research and diligence into a source-linked investment memo or decision record.

blocks.text: The companion can help the firm inspect the evidence and articulate its reasoning. The investment recommendation and decision still belong to the investors responsible for them.

Portfolio monitoring becomes useful when the firm agrees on what would actually matter. A financing, leadership change, product launch, customer signal, regulatory issue, or market shift may deserve attention; repeated coverage of the same announcement usually does not.

Strawberry can compare current signals with the last reliable company view, then carry meaningful changes into a board brief, portfolio update, open commitment, or useful introduction. Start with one review. A Routine makes sense only after the sources and signal rules hold up.

items.title: See what changed
items.text: Check current company and market signals against a reliable baseline and explain what may matter.

skill.context: Review meaningful portfolio-company changes against a reliable baseline and monitoring bar.

items.title: Prepare the portfolio update
items.text: Turn the reviewed company or portfolio picture into a concise update for the right audience.

skill.context: Turn reviewed company or portfolio context into a concise update for the right audience.

items.title: Close the important open loops
items.text: Find commitments, ownership gaps, and conflicting status across the places the work happened.

skill.context: Reconcile commitments, ownership, and conflicting status across portfolio or firm work.

sections.title: Teach the companion how the firm invests

blocks.text: The firm's edge lives in how it interprets its thesis, which sources it trusts, why it passes, which questions it asks, and how it builds conviction. As the team corrects real work, the companion can remember those choices so the next search, company brief, or memo starts closer to the firm's way of working.

items: Share an approved result when someone only needs the artifact.
Save a firm skill when the team should reuse the same sources, judgment, and review points.
Use a shared companion when several workflows need the same ongoing context.
Create a Routine after the trigger, sources, destination, and stop conditions are clear.
